subject: Hosting eligibility & evidence — next steps for WellGrid integration
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@wellgrid.health>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@wellgrid.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting eligibility & evidence — next steps for WellGrid integration

Thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion today — appreciated the clarity on the PHI use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the security call: 

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Data class: PHI (covered under HIPAA) — you confirmed patient identifiers and clinical notes will be persisted.
- Mandatory: BAA execution, SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit log retention (~12 months), encryption at rest + in transit, KMS integration (BYOK possibility).
- Operational: target p95 latency <300ms, steady QPS ~10–20, peak bursts to 50s of rps.
- Region: US-only data residency.

Quick hosting guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live and easiest for iteration but we cannot sign customer BAAs for shared-hosted offerings in current policy; SOC2 report available.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): supports BAA for customers with a committed plan; provides tenant isolation and can meet logging/retention and KMS requirements with some configuration.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): recommended when compliance requires strict network isolation, customer-controlled KMS/HSM, or on-premises audits. Supports full BAA and controls but involves longer provisioning and higher TCO.

Open questions for WellGrid to confirm (these will determine recommended path):
1) Do you require us to sign a BAA before any data flows are sent to Redwood (yes/no)?
2) Will you require BYOK (your KMS) or is Redwood KMS acceptable?
3) Are annual on-site audits expected from your side or third-party attestations sufficient?
4) Expected retention for logs/audit exports beyond application data (12 months by default?)
5) Any regulatory constraints beyond HIPAA (state laws, e.g., Massachusetts)?

Attachments included with this email: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (summary), BAA_template_Redwood.docx (starter), inference_arch_diagram.png (high-level).

Proposed next step: security + solutions deep-dive to walk through the checklist and map to hosting modes. Are you available Tuesday, 25 May between 10:00–11:00 PT? If you confirm preferred hosting mode on the call (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), we’ll produce an evidence pack and a preliminary pricing impact that same week.

Thanks — I’ll book a placeholder and circulate a short agenda once you confirm time.

—
Aisha Rahman

Subject: Re: Hosting eligibility & evidence — next steps for WellGrid integration

Aisha — thanks for the concise recap. A few items to clarify from our side: 
- Confirming PHI scope — yes, both identifiers and notes. BAA required.
- Preferred path: Private VPC is our preference for any production PHI workload, but we’re sensitive to lead time and cost; Dedicated might be acceptable if you can guarantee the isolation controls and sign the BAA.
- Traffic estimate: steady ~10–20 rps, peaks up to 50 rps for batch uploads. Latency target p95 <300ms.
- Log retention: 12 months for audit logs; application data retention negotiated separately.
- BYOK: we prefer BYOK for production (likely our cloud KMS).

Can you send a short matrix that maps our checklist items (BAA, SOC2, BYOK, audit logs, on-site audit) to each hosting option and the expected lead time? That will help our procurement and security teams decide.

Available for the Tue 5/25 slot you suggested — Priya and I will join.

Best,
John
Head of Product, WellGrid Health
john.lee@wellgrid.health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@wellgrid.health>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@wellgrid.health>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting eligibility & evidence — next steps for WellGrid integration

John — thanks, this is helpful. High-level mapping and what we can provide quickly: 

1) Hosted API
- BAA: NOT available for shared-hosted plans (policy).
- SOC2: Redwood SOC 2 Type II report available (we can provide redacted summary immediately).
- BYOK: not supported on hosted shared tiers.
- Lead time: minutes to enable (if you opt to experiment with non-PHI data).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- BAA: Yes — we can execute a BAA for Dedicated contracts.
- SOC2: report available; additional tenant-specific attestations possible via contract addendum.
- BYOK: supported in many Dedicated deployments (requires config and KMS agreement).
- Audit logs: configurable exports, default 12 months retention; custom retention possible.
- Lead time: typically 3–6 weeks for provisioning + contractual steps.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- BAA: Yes, full support.
- SOC2: we provide the same Type II evidence; for on-prem deployments, we support joint audit windows as required.
- BYOK / HSM: supported; you can bring keys and control them.
- Lead time: 6–12 weeks depending on network and onboarding.

Evidence package we will have ready for the call: SOC2 summary, BAA template, infra diagram showing network/KMS options, pen-test summary, and an itemized checklist tying each control to hosting options. I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and infra diagram to this thread (see aisha’s original attachments).

Two follow-ups for you to confirm before the call so we can tailor the agenda:
- Do you require an on-site audit or will a third-party attestation + remote evidence be sufficient?
- Any special encrypted egress restrictions (e.g., no external backups outside US)?

Agenda for Tue 5/25 (30–45m):
- 5m: objectives and timeline
- 15m: requirement-to-hosting mapping (BAA, BYOK, logs, audits)
- 10m: provisioning timeline & pricing impact by option
- 5–10m: next steps + decision checkpoints

If that looks good I’ll send a calendar invite and a 1-page pre-read mapping table to circulate to your security/procurement folks.

—
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
